# Bundled Python and MCP packages

GitHub Actions downloads the official Windows x64 CPython embeddable ZIP pinned in
`config/offline-artifacts.lock.json`. It modifies only `python313._pth` to expose
the bundled server and packages. CPython's original `LICENSE.txt` is retained in
the runtime and copied here as `PYTHON-LICENSE.txt` during packaging.

Python dependencies are pinned with SHA-256 hashes in
`config/redis/requirements.lock`. CI downloads binary wheels and installs them
into `runtime/python/Lib/site-packages`; no pip or package installation is needed
on the offline PC. All wheel license files and `.dist-info` metadata are retained.

The Word MCP server (word-mcp-live, MIT) needs mcp 2 through fastmcp 4, so its
dependencies are pinned separately in `config/word/requirements.lock` (copied here
as `word-requirements.lock`) and installed into `runtime/word-mcp`. Its launcher,
`mcp/word/word_mcp.py`, puts only that folder on the module path.
Windows-MCP 0.8.5 (MIT) uses the same embedded Python 3.13 with separate packages
in `runtime/windows-mcp`, selected by `mcp/windows/windows_mcp_launcher.py`.
`config/windows/requirements.lock` pins these dependencies and is copied here as
`windows-requirements.lock`. The original wheel licenses and metadata remain in that folder.
`PACKAGES.json`, generated by CI, identifies the installed metadata files of all three
package folders and their hashes. The manifest of the complete ZIP covers every runtime file.

Upstreams: https://www.python.org/, https://github.com/redis/redis-py,
https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk, https://github.com/ykarapazar/word-mcp-live,
https://github.com/CursorTouch/Windows-MCP.
Kilo starts the servers through
its built-in MCP support (`kilo.json`, written by setup.ps1); no separate MCP client is bundled.

Real server mappings, owner mappings, credentials, sessions, and caches are not
part of the release ZIP.
